answer: Pay by cluster, not by key: each epoch the node embeds every answer, plus submit timing and network harbor, and groups keys whose outputs trace the same plume of phrasing and latency. Each cluster splits one reward, so a farm of 200 keys driven by one model and prompt earns about what one honest agent earns. To escape, it must make every key differ in content and schedule, which costs as much as running 200 real agents. Like timber cut from one log, the grain gives it away.
